name: Branch Manager
label: Dischord
lede: A trio from a planned suburb twenty miles out of DC, two Dischord albums, one with Ian MacKaye at the mixing desk, and a tour so rough it ended the band.

eras.title: Big in Reston
eras.text: Branch Manager came out of Reston, Virginia, a planned community about 20 miles west of Washington. Dischord says they had made a name there and were starting to make an impact in DC by the early 1990s, with a following that stayed devoted.

years.h: Branch Manager forms in Reston, Virginia
years.p: [[Ron Winters|0829b0f9-1629-4099-9602-353940c33422]] on guitar and lead vocals, [[Dave Allen|f0f0d560-560b-4d40-883e-b795105446d0]] on bass and vocals, [[Derrick Decker|34dc89bf-5466-4563-a404-1599f96adbff]] on drums. AllMusic dates the start to 1990.
years.xp:
Reston was built in the 1960s as a model suburb, a long way in spirit from the DC punk houses. Dischord's history says the band built a name there first, then started to register in the city.

AllMusic hears [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] and [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] in them, but a wider range of influences than most of their label mates.

years.h: Branch Manager's first show, DC Space, January 6, 1991
yt: Branch Manager's first show, DC Space, January 6, 1991

years.h: Branch Manager singles on VHF and Level
years.p: Before Dischord, Branch Manager put out singles on VHF Records and Level Records.

eras.title: Onto the Dischord train
eras.text: The self-titled debut put a suburban trio on the same label as Fugazi and Jawbox. It sounded like neither, which AllMusic argues was both their strength and their problem.

years.h: Branch Manager's self-titled debut · Dischord No. 95
years.p: Eleven songs, from "Bent Flagpole" to "Unemployed Ninja" to "Hate, Resentment, And Jealousy." The band's Bandcamp dates it September 1, 1995.

years.h: AllMusic: being a Dischord band cut both ways
years.p: AllMusic's verdict on Branch Manager: their label and locale probably kept them from being known as more than yet another Dischord band.

eras.title: Tribal, then tired
eras.text: The second album came with Ian MacKaye helping at the board. Then a punishing trip on the road finished what the records had started, and the band called it by December.

years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear Studios, mixed by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and the band. Nine songs, including "The Guacamole Act of 1917" and "Nathan's Pets & Auto Supplies."

years.h: Branch Manager break up after a grueling trip
years.p: Dischord says Branch Manager came apart after a particularly grueling trip in 1997, and the band disbanded that December, two albums and seven years in.
years.xp: Nobody has put the details of the trip on the record.

eras.title: Afterward
eras.text: Branch Manager stayed on Dischord's 20th-anniversary box, and Ron Winters kept playing.

years.p: Branch Manager take their place on the label's anniversary compilation, Dischord No. 125.

years.h: Ron Winters returns with Sons of Disobedience
years.p: Ron Winters' later band, Sons of Disobedience, releases a four-song EP, per Dischord.
